'''Kamo Shrine''' (鴨神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha|1=Setsumatsusha}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}) (Inner Shrine). It is located on the mid-slope of {{ill|Mount Dainichi (Ise)|ja|大日山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Dainichi (Ise)|1=Mount Dainichi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435625}}, and is considered the most challenging {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} to reach among the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/125 Shrines of Ise|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref name="gk">{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to Gakken|1=Gakken Plus Co., Ltd.|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q86741099}} (2013): p.69</ref>.

== Overview ==
{{ill|Kamo shrines|lt=Kamo shrines|lt=Kamo Shrine|ja|鴨神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo Shrine}} is located at 1398 Okatani, Yamaga, Tamaki Town, Watarai District, Mie Prefecture<ref name="sk1">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.201</ref>. It is one of the 13 auxiliary and subordinate shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) located in Tamaki Town and Ranks 4th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.9–11</ref>.

The "Kamo" in the shrine name was traditionally believed to refer to an old place name. However, archaeological progress at the {{ill|Saikū|en|Saikū|qid=Q150845|lt=Saikū|1=Saikū}} site has led to suggestions of a connection with the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan}}, who served as water administrators<ref name="sk9">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.199</ref>.

The shrine grounds cover an area of 15,018 m²<ref name="sk2">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.202</ref>. The shrine building is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} style with a wooden plank roof, facing south, and is enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|Tamagaki|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki|1=Sacred fences}}<ref name="sk2"/>. It features one {{ill|Shinmei torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|1=Torii|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk2"/>. The sacred object (shintai) is a stone<ref>Kaneko (1983): p.59</ref>. There is no offertory box.

A stream flowing beneath the shrine grounds is said to have never dried up, even during droughts<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.65</ref>. The trees on the grounds display beautiful autumn foliage during late autumn<ref name="ic"/>.

== Enshrined Deities ==
The enshrined deities are '''Ishikorowake no Mikoto''' (石己呂和居命) and '''Mimae no Kami''' (御前神)<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Both deities are children of {{ill|Ōminakami no Mikoto|ja|大水上命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and are considered gods of agriculture and irrigation<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Originally, there were separate shrine buildings for each deity<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.10</ref>, but after the shrine was restored by {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} during the Edo period, the deities have been enshrined together in a single structure<ref name="sk2"/>.

== History ==
According to the ''Enryaku Gishiki-chō'', the shrine was established during the reign of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}<ref>Kaneko (1983): p.68</ref>, giving it a history as long as the Ise Grand Shrine itself<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.200</ref>. In ancient texts, the shrine is referred to as "Kamo-sha" or "Kamo Jinja," and its reading as "Kamo" is undisputed<ref name="sk9"/>.

It was designated to undergo reconstruction every 20 years, following the tradition of the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|lt=Shikinen Sengū|ja|式年遷宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 遷宮}} at the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="sk0"/>. However, records of reconstruction ceased after an entry from December 8, 1340, which mentions an order to rebuild the shrine using rice tributes from Tajima Province<ref name="sk0"/>.

In 1663 (Kanbun 3), the shrine was restored by Grand Priest {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Yamaga Village, Okatani<ref name="sk0"/>. {{ill|Mikado Kiyonao|ja|御巫清直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikado Kiyonao|1=Mikannagi Kiyonao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6537624}} later criticized this restoration site as inappropriate in his work ''Ninomiya Kansha Engaku Kō'', proposing that the original site was within Yamaga Village at the remains of the former {{ill|Yahashira Shrine|lt=Yahashira Shrine|1=Hachioji Shrine|ja|八柱神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yahashira Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, which had been merged in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.201–202</ref>.

The current location was established in 1876 (Meiji 9)<ref name="sk0"/>. The shrine building was reconstructed in 1922 (Taishō 11)<ref name="uy"/>.

== Rituals ==
On the 16th day of the 3rd lunar month, a ritual known as ''Miyatamori Shinji'' (宮田もり神事) is held, which is associated with {{ill|Kōshin|en|Kōshin|qid=Q3082157|lt=Kōshin belief|1=Kōshin}}<ref>Sakurai (1991): p.293</ref>.

During the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}} (February), {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}} (October), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}} (November), rituals are conducted in front of the shrine. For the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai}} (January 1), {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January), {{ill|Kenkoku Kinen no Hi|ja|建国記念祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenkoku Kinen no Hi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (February 11), {{ill|Fūhi no Sai|ja|風日祈祭|1=Kazahi-no-Misai|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fūhi no Sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May and August), and {{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|1=The Emperor's Birthday|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (December 23), remote rituals are performed at the Gojōden of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.200–201</ref>.

== Access ==
Near the shrine are the ruins of an ancient icehouse (氷室) associated with the {{ill|Saikū|en|Saikū|qid=Q150845|lt=Saikū|1=Saikū}}<ref name="ic"/>. About 2.5 km from Kamo Shrine is the {{ill|Kamoshimo Shrine|ja|鴨下神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamoshimo Shrine}}, which enshrines the same deity and is located within the same Shirota region<ref name="sk0"/>.

; By Public Transport
There are no nearby train stations or bus stops. From {{ill|Tamaru Station|en|Tamaru Station|qid=Q117533|lt=Tamaru Station|1=Tamaru Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=JR Sangū Line|1=Sangū Line}}, it is about a 50-minute walk (4.0 km) southwest, or about 53 minutes (4.3 km) south from {{ill|Tokida Station|en|Tokida Station|qid=Q7813584|lt=Sotojōda Station|1=Tokida Station}}<ref name="ic"/>. From Yamaga village, a stone marker labeled "Kamo Shrine" leads through a bamboo grove, under a tunnel beneath the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway|1=Ise Expressway}}, and along a mountain path to the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. The distance from the marker to the shrine is about 1.1 km<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.63</ref>, taking around 20 minutes<ref name="gk"/>. There are forestry roads nearby, so caution is advised to avoid getting lost<ref name="ic"/>.

; By Car
From {{ill|Tamaki Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamaki Interchange|1=Tamaki interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11572465}} on the Ise Expressway, it takes about 6 minutes (2.1 km) to reach the stone marker for Kamo Shrine<ref name="gk"/>. The mountain path beyond the marker is for pedestrians only, and vehicles cannot pass through. However, there is a parking area near {{ill|Matoyama Park|ja|的山公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matoyama Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, which is accessible via a tunnel under the Ise Expressway. This route includes a paved mountain path, reducing the walking distance.
